problem:
Let $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 4 & k\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ where $k$ is a constant such that $k\ne 8.$ Which of the following statements are true?

- $det(A)\ne 0$
- The system $Ax=b$ has infinitely many solutions
- The lines $x+2y=2$ and $4x+ky=0$ don't intersect
worked_solution:
Recall that given $A=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{11} & {a}_{12} \\ {a}_{21} & {a}_{22}\end{aligned}]$, then according to the invertible matrix theorem the following statements are equivalent:    

- $A$ is invertible.

- The system $Ax=b$ has exactly one solution for any $2\times 1$ column vector $b.$

- The system $Ax=0$ has the unique zero solution.

- The lines ${a}_{11}x+{a}_{12}y={b}_{1}$ and ${a}_{21}x+{a}_{22}y={b}_{2}$ intersect at exactly one point.

- $det(A)\ne 0.$

With that in mind, let's now check our statements.

- Statement I is true. We have 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =det[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 4 & k\end{aligned}] \\  & =1\cdot k-2\cdot 4 \\  & =k-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $k-8\ne 0$ if $k\ne 8.$

Now, since the fifth part of the invertible matrix theorem is true, all the other parts of the theorem are true too. Therefore, according to the theorem:

- Statement II is false by the second part of the invertible matrix theorem.

- Statement III is false.  According to the fourth part of the invertible matrix theorem, the lines must intersect at exactly one point.

Finally, only statement I is true.
